correctness.rationale: Using the actual Nguyen–Nguyen–Dang–Do primary Eq.(10) Newton(F)=conv union_{i=0}^m S_m lambda^(i), Euclidean center uniqueness and full permutation symmetry force center c1. Layer squared-distance increments equal 2(beta_i-alpha_i)(h_i-c), h_i=(alpha_i+beta_i)/2 nonincreasing, so the maximum layer is coordinatewise farther endpoints and Φ(c)=Σ_j max[(alpha_j-c)^2,(beta_j-c)^2]. Φ is m-strongly convex, and on h_{i+1}≤c≤h_i its minimizer is the mixed-layer mean c_i; checking interval and boundary subderivative yields the complete unique O(m) scan. Strict convexity of ball excludes other boundary contact points. Independent exact Fraction checks on 300 deterministically generated valid weakly decreasing endpoint pairs and all m≤6 plus the (3,1,0),(3,3,3) example corroborate symbolic proof.
residual_risks: The source’s endpoint chain property is required, not valid for arbitrary symmetric polynomial.
Symmetry center argument uses Euclidean metric in exponent coordinates; tests bounded only.

value.rationale: Newton polytopes of good symmetric polynomials are a natural broad algebraic-combinatorial family, and Euclidean minimum enclosing sphere is a canonical geometric invariant independent of integer-decomposition/Ehrhart data. O(m) exact scalar evaluation plus all active contact orbits is reusable despite elementary convex-analytic ingredients; the inhomogeneous mixed-degree layers make this a meaningful classification rather than an arbitrary numerical table.
residual_risks: No claim about inradius, John ellipsoid, general polynomial families, or full face lattice.

final_claim: For every good symmetric polynomial with endpoint partitions alpha<=beta, Newton(F) has unique Euclidean minimum enclosing ball center c*1 and radius sqrt(Σ_j max{(alpha_j-c*)²,(beta_j-c*)²}), with c* from an O(m) endpoint-threshold/mean scan; contacts are active permutation orbits.
limitations: Tied to exact source good-polynomial chain and standard Euclidean exponent norm.
